news.title: Nations championship, Rugby League World Cup and NFL action – follow with us
news.lede: Here’s how to follow along with our coverage – the finest writing and up-to-the-minute reports. There will be plenty to talk about in the world of football on Saturday morning. As well as building up to Saturday’s four Premier League games, David Tindall will be looking at the fallout from Frank Lampard’s return to Everton with Coventry on Friday night and reaction to Thomas Tuchel’s last England squad of the year. But it’s also FA Cup first round proper day, when League One and League Two sides find themselves pitched against other lower-division sides or at risk of being giantkilled by non-league clubs.

news.title: 2 winners and 2 losers now Ben White is once again back with England
news.lede: On Friday morning, ahead of the upcoming international break, Thomas Tuchel named his England squad. The list contains five Arsenal players, which is more representatives than Liverpool, Chelsea, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham have combined, even with Bukayo Saka sidelined . Ezri Konsa, Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Eberechi Eze were not really surprise call ups, but Benjamin White's name did raise a few eyebrows . The 29 year old has just six caps to his name, but could add to that against Croatia at Wembley and then Spain in Madrid next week.So, we asses two winners and two losers following this news.

news.title: FIFA lawyer departs weeks after UEFA’s 42 questions on Infantino and disciplinary meddling
news.lede: GENEVA FIFA’s top lawyer left the body on Friday after eight years working for its president Gianni Infantino and a men’s World Cup in North America which drew intense scrutiny on disciplinary rulings. “Emilio García Silvero has expressed his wish to embark on a new chapter in his career and return to Spain after 15 years of working abroad in the service of international football,” FIFA said in a statement. As head of FIFA’s legal and compliance unit, García oversaw tournament disciplinary cases, transfer market rules and contractual disputes worldwide, and steered moving the body’s lawyers from Zurich to Miami in 2023.

news.title: Spain should withdraw from 2030 World Cup if not given final: opposition leader
news.lede: “The final of the World Cup must be held where it is fair, where it is appropriate, where it is beyond question: in Spain,” said Alberto Nunez Feijoo in an interview with Spanish television programme El Chiringuito late on Thursday. Asked whether he would advocate Spain, whose national team won this year’s World Cup, withdrawing from the joint tournament if Morocco was awarded the final, he replied: “Yes. In a post on X on Friday, Feijoo said: “You do not humiliate international football’s leading power.” The three host nations of the 2030 tournament are competing to stage the final, with Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu stadium and a planned 115,000-seat venue in Benslimane, near Casablanca, seen as the leading contenders.

news.title: FIFA World Cup 2030: Spain opposition leader threatens withdrawal if Morocco hosts final
news.lede: CHENNAI Spanish opposition leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo has called for Spain to withdraw from co-hosting the 2030 FIFA World Cup if Morocco is chosen to stage the final. Spain, Portugal and Morocco will jointly host the tournament, but FIFA has yet to decide which country will stage the title clash. Feijoo heads the conservative Popular Party, insisted during an interview with Spanish television programme El Chiringuito on Thursday that Spain deserved to host the final. He also confirmed that he would seek to withdraw Spain from organising the tournament if he were in power and FIFA awarded the final to Morocco.

news.title: Feijoo says Spain should withdraw as host if World Cup final goes to Morocco
news.lede: Leader of the opposition and the People's Party, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, speaks at the headquarters of People's Party (PP) in Madrid, Spain October 5, 2026. BARCELONA, Nov 6 - Spanish opposition leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo says he would be willing to withdraw Spain as a host of the 2030 World Cup should FIFA award the final to Morocco, amid a fierce battle between the two countries to accommodate football's biggest match. FIFA are yet to declare a venue for the final of the 2030 World Cup, hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain. Feijoo, who leads the conservative Popular Party, said on Thursday that it was "inarguable" that Spain should host the event.

news.title: A surprise: Inzaghi to lead Al-Hilal in the 2029 Club World Cup!
news.lede: The Italian coach has not renewed his contract so far. A Saudi journalist has dropped a major bombshell, confirming that Al-Hilal manager Simone Inzaghi will lead the Italian into the 2029 FIFA Club World Cup. Reports had suggested Al-Hilal's management put Inzaghi under observation to settle whether he would stay on, particularly after defeats to Neom in the Roshn League and Qatar's Al-Shamal in the AFC Champions League Elite. Saudi journalist Abdulaziz Al-Muraisel told "Nabd Tuwaiq" otherwise.

news.title: Men's World Cup: Mexico's most creative football pitches
news.lede: On the southern outskirts of Mexico City, amateur teams meet on a very unique football pitch every Sunday. Known as the "Field of the Gods," it is perched inside the extinct Teoca volcano and situated a breathtaking 2,700 meters (8,800 feet) above sea level. The pitch was created by the nearby community more than 60 years ago and is a source of local pride. Cars above, sports below: this pitch in Mexico City's colorful Las Aguilas neighborhood gives people the space to play soccer beneath a highway overpass.
